name: Hip Abduction Machine
description: The hip abduction machine provides seated, bilateral hip abduction against a weight stack, targeting the gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, and tensor fasciae latae. The seated position eliminates balance demands and allows the abductors to be loaded in isolation through a full controlled range of motion. It is a popular machine exercise for developing lateral hip width and stability.

execution.starting_position: Sit in the hip abduction machine with back against the pad, knees against the inner pads, and feet on the footrests. Adjust the pads to a comfortable starting position.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat and pad width to a comfortable range. Set weight stack to a load that allows full range motion with control.
steps: Step 1: Sit in the machine with back flat against the pad. Place knees against the inner surfaces of the pads.
Step 2: Push both knees apart — abducting the hips — against the pad resistance.
Step 3: Push until the pads reach the end of range or until maximum comfortable abduction.
Step 4: Hold the peak position briefly.
Step 5: Return the knees inward under control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you push the knees apart. Inhale as you bring them back.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight, which causes the torso to lean or the lower back to arch
Releasing the tension too quickly on the return — control the eccentric
Not adjusting the pad to a comfortable starting range
safety_considerations: Low risk when performed with appropriate weight
Avoid if the exercise causes hip or groin pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Push the knees as far apart as the machine allows or until comfortable. Full excursion of the pads.
coaching_cues: Push through the outer knees — not just the thighs
Control the return — don't let the weight snap back
Keep the back flat against the pad
